1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.
16	
17	### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not
18	
19	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`
20	
21	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
22	comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
23	enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.
24	
25	A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
26	grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
27	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.
28	
29	**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
30	or drop the claim from the doc comment.
31	
32	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
33	
34	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
35	
36	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
37	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
38	
39	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
40	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
41	than a drive-by fix.
42	
43	### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`
44	
45	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`
46	
47	After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
48	`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
49	`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.
50	
51	Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
52	happen and is misleading to read.
53	
54	### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths
55	
56	`internal/oci/oci.go:262`
57	
58	Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
59	member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
60	references.
61	
62	**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
63	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
64	actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.
65	
66	Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
67	under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
68	`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.
69	
70	**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
71	them.
72	
73	### 1.1 Fixed
74	
75	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
76	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
77	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
78	
79	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
80	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
81	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
82	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
83	ones.
84	
85	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
86	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
87	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
88	gone.
89	
90	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
91	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
92	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
93	
94	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
95	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
96	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
97	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
98	
99	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
100	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
101	
102	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
103	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
104	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
105	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
106	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
107	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
108	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
109	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
110	
111	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
112	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
113	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
114	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
115	
116	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
117	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
118	contexts anyway.
119	
120	Two smaller defects went with it:
121	
122	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
123	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
124	  hang indefinitely.
125	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
126	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
127	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
128	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
129	
130	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
131	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
132	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
133	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
134	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
135	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
136

139	## 2. Technical debt
140	
141	### Test coverage
142	
143	Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
144	**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.
145	
146	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
147	
148	| Phase | Scope | Status |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
151	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
152	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
153	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
154	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
155	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
156	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |
157	
158	Phase 1 progress:
159	
160	| Package | Before | Now |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
163	| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
164	| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
165	| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
166	| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
167	| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
168	| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
169	| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |
170	
171	`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
172	paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
173	`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
174	single-response stubs used so far.
175	
176	Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
177	invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
178	drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
179	`app` remain.
180	
181	`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
182	built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
183	the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
184	rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.
185	
186	`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
187	through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
188	`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
189	throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
190	real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
191	would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
192	installing a credential helper that sleeps.
193	
194	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
195	
196	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:
197	
198	| File | Lines |
199	|---|---|
200	| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
201	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
202	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
203	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
204	| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
205	| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
206	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
207	
208	`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
209	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
210	`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
211	is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
212	host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
213	free for the `docker network` family.
214	
215	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
216	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
217	Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
218	7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.
219	
220	### Race detector cannot run locally
221	
222	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
223	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
224	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
225	
226	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
227	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
228	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
229	
230	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
231	tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
232	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
233	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
234	
235	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
236	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

240	## 3. Planned features
241	
242	Carried over from `todo.md`.
243	
244	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
245	
246	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
247	  redirections to the host machine.
248	
249	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
250	
251	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
252	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
253	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
254	  directly into the Workspace view.
255	
256	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
257	
258	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
259	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
260	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
261	    the Docker daemon).
262	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
263	    downloading the whole image.
264	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
265	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
266	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
267	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
268	
269	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
270	
271	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
272	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
273	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
274	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
275	
276	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
277	
278	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
279	  for every container in the selected project.
280	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
281	
282	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
283	
284	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
285	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
286	switching context.
287	
288	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
289	not a chosen design.
290	
291	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
292	
293	| Surface | Size |
294	|---|---|
295	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
296	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
297	
298	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
299	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
300	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
301	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
302	
303	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
304	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
305	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
306	`shared.GitLabStats`.
307	
308	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
309	
310	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
311	promise.
312	
313	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
314	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
315	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
316	  backend declares.
317	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
318	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
319	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
320	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
321	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
322	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
323	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
324	  limits and semantics.
325	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
326	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
327	  applies either way.
328	
329	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
330	
331	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
332	package needs a seam.
333	
334	Arguments for the CLIs:
335	
336	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
337	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
338	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
339	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
340	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
341	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
342	
343	Arguments against:
344	
345	- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
346	  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
347	  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
348	  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
349	  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
350	  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
351	  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
352	- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
353	  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
354	  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
355	- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
356	  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
357	  paginates.
358	- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
359	  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
360	  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
361	  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
362	  rather than testing against it.
363	
364	**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
365	surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
366	no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
367	`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
368	a recommendation, not a decision.
369	
370	#### Sketch of the work
371	
372	1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
373	   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
374	   dashboard counters, clone URL.
375	2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
376	   the other 65 call sites follow from.
377	3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
378	   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
379	4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
380	   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
381	5. Implement the GitHub backend.
382	6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
383	   memory survives.
384	
385	Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
386	tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.
387	
388	---
389

394	
395	- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
396	  — Docker-layer platform portability.

421	// wrapLines soft-wraps content so no line exceeds width runes.
422	func wrapLines(content string, width int) string {
423		if width <= 0 {
424			return content
425		}
426		lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
427		out := make([]string, 0, len(lines))
428		for _, line := range lines {
429			runes := []rune(line)
430			if len(runes) <= width {
431				out = append(out, line)
432				continue
433			}
434			for len(runes) > width {
435				out = append(out, string(runes[:width]))
436				runes = runes[width:]
437			}
438			if len(runes) > 0 {
439				out = append(out, string(runes))
440			}
441		}
442		return strings.Join(out, "\n")
443	}

633		copy(sorted, containers)

635		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
636			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]

638			var less bool
639			switch m.sortColumn {
640			case sortByImage:
641				less = strings.ToLower(a.Image) < strings.ToLower(b.Image)
642			case sortByCPU:
643				less = a.CPUPercent < b.CPUPercent
644			case sortByMem:
645				less = a.MemPercent < b.MemPercent
646			case sortByNetRX:
647				less = a.NetRX < b.NetRX
648			case sortByNetTX:

650			case sortByBlockRX:
651				less = a.BlockRX < b.BlockRX
652			case sortByBlockTX:
653				less = a.BlockTX < b.BlockTX
654			case sortByCreated:
655				less = a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
656			default: // sortByName

662			}

701	// formatMemUsage parses docker MemUsage "150MiB / 7.776GiB" into compact "150M/8G"
702	func formatMemUsage(memUsage string) string {
703		parts := strings.SplitN(memUsage, "/", 2)
704		if len(parts) != 2 {
705			return memUsage
706		}
707		used := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
708		total := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
709		return used + "/" + total
710	}

712	// formatMemValue converts "150MiB" -> "150M", "7.776GiB" -> "8G", "512KiB" -> "512K"
713	func formatMemValue(val string) string {
714		val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
715	
716		// Try each unit suffix
717		for _, suffix := range []struct {
718			docker string
719			short  string
720			isGig  bool
721		}{
722			{"GiB", "G", true},
723			{"MiB", "M", false},
724			{"KiB", "K", false},
725			{"B", "B", false},
726		} {
727			if strings.HasSuffix(val, suffix.docker) {
728				numStr := strings.TrimSuffix(val, suffix.docker)
729				num, err := strconv.ParseFloat(numStr, 64)
730				if err != nil {
731					return val
732				}
733				if suffix.isGig {
734					// Round GiB to nearest integer
735					return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
736				}
737				// For MiB/KiB, show integer
738				return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
739			}
740		}
741		return val
742	}

752			if err != nil {
753				return createdAt

documents: constructors are pure and `Update()` is a pure function, so feeding
synthetic messages fully determines the resulting state. No test executes a
command Update returns — they shell out to Docker, hit the GitLab API, sleep for
a second or open a browser — so the assertions are on model state instead. The
few places that must touch disk (`config.Load` after a save, `config.Save`)
redirect `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` at a temporary directory, the same trick
`internal/credentials` uses.

Three constraints the phase surfaced, worth knowing before phases 3–5:

- **Colour has to be forced to test styling.** Under `go test` lipgloss detects
  no TTY, falls back to the Ascii profile and strips every escape sequence — so
  any assertion about colour passes whatever the code does. `containers` calls
  `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` for the tests that need it and
  restores it afterwards; that is what makes the Rule 122 check (no escape
  sequences in `table.Row` cells) real rather than vacuous. Verified by styling
  a cell on purpose and watching the test fail. `termenv` moved to a direct
  dependency for this.
- **`bubbles/table` keeps its styles unexported**, so `refreshSelectionStyle` is
  asserted by looking for the error-selection escape sequence in the rendered
  table rather than by reading `Styles()`.
- **`sort.Slice` is not stable**, so fixtures must give every sortable column a
  total order or the expected sequences are ambiguous.

Two handlers are deliberately left uncovered in `containers`: `s` and `S` call
`detectShell`, which runs `docker exec` synchronously *inside* `Update`. The
tests drive those keys only in states that return before reaching it. The same
shape appears in `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`, which calls `config.Load()` from
`Update`. Neither is a Rule 110 violation — nothing mutates the model from a
`Cmd` — but I/O in `Update` blocks the event loop and is untestable without a
seam. Worth a look when phase 5 gets to the router.

**Sur la question de branche** : pas besoin de repasser par `main` quand les changements sont indépendants. Là j'ai fait une seule branche, un commit par paquet, une PR — repasser par `main` n'a d'intérêt que si un changement dépend du précédent (ou si tu veux mergerdans un ordre précis).

**Phase 2 terminée** : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/13 (CI verte, `test-race` inclus)

| Paquet | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/containers` | 0 % | **87,2 %** |
| `internal/ui/dashboard` | 0 % | **81,5 %** |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/auth` | 0 % | **94,5 %** |
| **global** | 18,2 % | **30,8 %** |

Avec `status` (#12), les cinq paquets de la phase 2 sont tous au-dessus de 80 %.

**Le point qui m'a fait revenir en arrière** : sous `go test`, lipgloss ne détecte pas de TTY, retombe sur le profil Ascii et supprime toutes les séquences d'échappement. Le test Rule 122 que j'avais écrit en #12 (« pas d'ANSI dans les cellules ») passait donc **quoi que fasse le code**. Il force maintenant `termenv.TrueColor` le temps du test — vérifié en stylant une cellule exprès pour voir l'échec. Ça permet aussi d'attester `refreshSelectionStyle`, puisque `bubbles` garde ses styles non exportés : le test cherche la séquence de sélection « erreur » dans le rendu.

**Deux trouvailles :**
- *Corrigé* — l'aide de containers annonçait `S` (shell en nouvelle fenêtre) sans le documenter, même dérive que `n`/`ctrl+n` sur status. Chaque paquet vérifie désormais que toute touche de `GetShortcuts()` figure dans `GetHelpContent()`.
- *Enregistré en D9* — `containers.New()` laisse `sortAsc` à sa valeur zéro : la liste s'ouvre triée **Z→A**, alors que status s'ouvre A→Z. L'en-tête affiche bien `Name ▼`, donc la vue est honnête, mais personne ne l'a choisi. Épinglé par un test plutôt que corrigé — ça change ce que tu vois à l'ouverture, c'est ton arbitrage (une ligne).

**Non couvert volontairement** : `s`/`S` dans containers appellent `detectShell`, qui lance `docker exec` **synchrone dans `Update`**. Même forme que `config.Load()` dans `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`. Ce n'est pas une violation de la Rule 110 — rien ne mute le modèle depuis un `Cmd` — mais ça bloque la boucle d'événements et il faut un seam pour tester. Noté au backlog pour la phase 5.

Prochaine étape possible : phase 3 (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`, ~2 470 stmts) — mais trois de ces fichiers dépassent 800 lignes, donc c'est là que la tension « tester avant de découper » du backlog devient réelle.
